question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 4}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-8}{{x}^{2}+x-20} & =\frac{{4}^{2}-2(4)-8}{{4}^{2}+4-20}=\frac{0}{0},\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-8}{{x}^{2}+x-20} & =\frac{(x+2)(x-4)}{(x+5)(x-4)} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{x+5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 4}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-8}{{x}^{2}+x-20} & ={lim}_{x\to 4}\frac{x+2}{x+5} \\  & =\frac{4+2}{4+5} \\  & =\frac{6}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
